source.purpose: Reference database for PSLE Science answering, key vocabulary, model reasoning patterns and topic coverage. This source informs application marking and training-model generation but must not silently replace the existing 89 memorisation sentences unless explicitly approved.

answering_principles.rule: For adaptation questions, identify WHAT the adaptation is, explain HOW it works, then explain WHY it helps the organism survive by linking to a CROP purpose: coping with physical factors, reproduction, obtaining food or protection/escape.

For human-impact questions, state the human action, the environmental change it causes, and the resulting effect on organisms or habitats. For conservation questions, state the action and the environmental benefit.

When using an observation to identify a property of matter or a material, quote the observation first and link it to the exact property, such as occupies space, can be compressed, fixed shape, fixed volume, transparency, strength, flexibility or ability to float/sink.

For condensation explanations, identify the source of the water vapour, state that it contacts a cooler surface or cooler air, loses heat, then condenses into tiny water droplets. Do not imply that the visible droplets came through a container wall unless the scenario states so.
For rate-of-evaporation questions, identify the changed factor and state the direction of change in evaporation rate. Main factors shown are wind, exposed surface area and temperature.

For shadow-size questions, compare the relative positions of light source, object and screen before stating the resulting shadow size. Moving the object nearer the light source generally makes the shadow larger; moving it nearer the screen generally makes the shadow smaller.

key_ideas: Adaptations may be structural or behavioural.
The book groups survival purposes using CROP: coping with physical factors, reproduction, obtaining food and protection/escape.
Examples of animal adaptations include migration, hibernation, camouflage, group behaviour, body coverings and specialised feeding structures.
Examples of plant adaptations include leaf changes for reducing water loss, storage structures, aerial roots/pneumatophores and fruit/seed structures for reproduction.
Human actions can have negative or positive impacts on the environment.
answer_patterns: WHAT adaptation -> HOW it works -> WHY it improves survival
Human action -> environmental change -> effect on organisms/habitat

key_ideas: Pollution can affect air, water and land.
Deforestation can destroy habitats and reduce food/shelter, leading to population decline or extinction risk.
Global warming is linked in the book to increased carbon dioxide, heat trapping, melting ice and sea-level rise.
Depletion of natural resources occurs when resources are used faster than they can be replenished.
Positive actions include conservation, reforestation, managing invasive species and sustainable habits such as reduce, reuse and recycle.
Matter has mass and occupies space.
Solids have definite shape and definite volume.
Liquids have no definite shape but have definite volume and take the shape of their container.
Gases have no definite shape and no definite volume and can be compressed.
Air can be used as evidence that gas occupies space and can be compressed.
Mass and volume can be measured using suitable apparatus such as balances and measuring cylinders.
application_patterns: Syringe plunger can move inward -> trapped air can be compressed.
Air prevents another substance/object from occupying the same space -> air occupies space.
Liquid changes container shape while volume remains the same -> liquid has no fixed shape but fixed volume.

topics.topic: Cycles in water and changes of state
key_ideas: Melting and boiling involve heat gain; freezing and condensation involve heat loss.
Evaporation can occur at any temperature and only at the surface of a liquid.
Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at the boiling point.
Main factors affecting evaporation rate shown are wind, exposed surface area and temperature.
Condensation occurs when water vapour loses heat and changes into liquid water.
Water cycle processes shown include evaporation, condensation and precipitation.
Water is important to humans and plants, and water conservation reduces unnecessary use.

sequence: Water vapour contacts cooler surface or cooler air
common_scenarios: Droplets on outside of a cold container: water vapour from surrounding air condenses on cooler outer surface.
Droplets on underside of a lid/cover: water vapour from warm object/liquid condenses on the cooler surface.
Mist near a cold object: surrounding air is cooled; water vapour condenses into tiny droplets in the air.
Steam/mist near hot water: hot water forms water vapour; when it reaches cooler air it loses heat and condenses into tiny droplets.

key_ideas: Properties shown include waterproofness, conductivity, magnetism, flexibility, ability to float/sink, strength and transparency.
Material choice should be justified using the required property and the function of the object.
topics.answer_pattern: Required function -> relevant material property -> why that property suits the use

key_ideas: Light is a form of energy that enables us to see.
Light travels in straight lines.
Light can be reflected.
We see an object when light reflected from the object enters our eyes.
Transparent materials allow most light through, translucent materials allow some light through, and opaque materials do not allow light through.
A shadow forms when light is partially or completely blocked by an object.
Shadow size depends on the relative positions of the light source, object and screen.
shadow_relationships: Object nearer light source -> larger shadow.
Light source farther from object -> shadow can become larger in the book's illustrated setup.
